# `Q-25-6` — Invalid component option value

> A component's `bind` is not `#id` or `.class`, or its `content` is not `dom`, `ast` or `none`. The entry is skipped.

## What this means

Two options take a fixed vocabulary. `bind` is a selector of exactly one
of two forms, `#id` or `.class`; `content` chooses how the element's
content reaches the component: `dom` (the default: the rendered markup is
handed back as `children`), `ast` (the node's Pandoc AST is attached as
JSON and arrives as `node`), or `none`. Any other value is this warning,
and the entry is skipped.

## Why this happens

- `bind:` is a general CSS selector (`div.card`, `#a > p`), which is not
  supported: bindings are resolved on the document tree at render time,
  where only ids and classes are known.
- `bind:` has a space or a second `#`/`.` in it.
- `bind: chrome`, which is reserved for the components Quarto declares
  itself for page chrome (`toc-component`); an author's entry binds with
  `#id` or `.class`.
- `content:` is misspelled or capitalized.

## How to fix

Write `bind: "#some-id"` (quoted, since `#` starts a YAML comment) or
`bind: .some-class`, and one of `content: dom`, `content: ast`,
`content: none`.

## Related

- The components guide (`docs/guides/authoring/components.qmd`) describes
  the `components:` key, the element contract and the runtime.
